name: Hotwind Youth Club
tagline: A little curiosity. A lot of possibility.
从一点好奇，走向更多可能。
intro: A student-led community bringing people together through reading, discussion and shared activities.
一个由学生发起的社群，通过阅读、讨论与共同活动连接彼此。

label: activities organised
场线上线下活动
note: Across reading, dialogue and health communication
涵盖阅读、对话与健康传播

label: weeks of shared reading
周线上共读计划
note: Approximate total reported by the founder
创始人提供的累计周数估计

label: people in the core team
位核心团队成员
note: A small team with shared responsibilities
共同分工、共同建设的小团队

title: Start with a reading salon
从一场读书沙龙开始
text: I started Hotwind to offer university students a more open space to read, exchange ideas and meet beyond formal coursework.
我发起热風，希望为大学生提供一个更开放的空间，在课程之外阅读、交流与相遇。
lesson: Begin with a need you can see.
从身边真实的需求出发。

title: Test a bigger idea
试验更大的可能
text: An innovation project became a way to explore the relationship between reading, peer support and youth development.
通过创新项目，我们开始探索阅读、朋辈支持与青年成长之间的联系。
lesson: An early idea is something to test.
最初的想法，需要在实践中检验。

title: Reflect, then rebuild
反思边界，重新搭建
text: After reviewing early ideas about peer support, we refocused the community on reading, discussion and public engagement. Peer exchange remained distinct from professional psychological services.
回顾早期关于朋辈支持的构想后，我们把社群重新聚焦于阅读、讨论与公众参与，并明确朋辈交流与专业心理服务的边界。
lesson: 倾听，也意味着愿意调整方向。

title: Explore wider connections
探索更广泛的连接
text: We explored contacts with academic, cultural, public-interest and life-science groups in Chongqing and Wuhan.
我们尝试与重庆、武汉的学术、文化、公益和生命科学社群建立联系。
lesson: 让共同关心的问题，成为连接的起点。

label: READING & CONNECTION
阅读与连接
title: Reading, shared discussion and collective writing
阅读、共读讨论与集体创作
summary: Reading salons and the Changliu programme combined individual reading, online check-ins and group discussion.
通过读书会与长流计划，结合个人阅读、线上打卡与集体交流。
question: What if reading were a starting point for connection?
如果阅读，也能成为人与人连接的起点？
why: I wanted a place where students could exchange ideas beyond coursework and have conversations with enough time and trust to go deeper.
我希望大家在课程之外也能交换想法，在有时间、有信任的交流中，把一个问题讨论得更深入。

title: Read and keep a record
阅读与记录
text: Programme posters invited participants to choose a book, record their progress and share short reading reflections.
项目海报邀请参与者选择书籍、记录阅读进度，并分享简短的阅读体会。

title: Exchange ideas
交流阅读所得
text: The 2024 guide proposed online voice conversations and an in-person discussion at the end of the reading cycle.
2024年项目说明安排了线上语音交流与周期末的线下阅读讨论。

title: Write and share together
共同创作与分享
text: The May 2025 materials describe combining participants’ writing into a shared work. Photographs record the closing sharing session.
2025年5月材料介绍了汇集参与者文字、合成共同作品的形式；照片记录了最后的分享环节。

role: I founded the community and coordinated its development with the core team, helping turn informal interest into a recurring programme.
我发起社群，与核心团队共同协调发展，把最初的阅读兴趣逐步转化为持续开展的活动。
reflection: Repeated opportunities to read and discuss were central to the programme’s design. Its duration is not evidence of participant retention or measured learning gains.
持续提供阅读与交流的机会，是项目设计的重要部分；项目时长本身不代表参与者留存率或已测量的学习提升。
evidenceNote: Photographs document selected sessions. Programme posters describe the intended format; the founder reports around 20 weeks of shared reading overall.
照片记录部分活动现场，项目海报介绍当期设计；累计约20周的共读时长由创始人提供。

label: PLAY & PUBLIC HEALTH
游戏与公共健康
title: Tuberculosis awareness through a mystery game
通过剧本游戏，开展结核病科普。
summary: The event materials combine a fictional hospital mystery, a medical-themed social deduction game and a short session on tuberculosis awareness.
活动材料将虚构的医院谜案、医学主题社交推理游戏与简短的结核病科普环节结合。
question: How could health education invite people to participate?
怎样让健康科普，更愿意被主动参与？
why: The activity used a fictional hospital mystery as an introduction to a health topic for participants without specialist training. The accompanying science session was intended to introduce tuberculosis awareness.
活动以虚构的医院谜案为没有专业训练的参与者提供入口，并安排简短科普来介绍结核病相关知识。

title: Follow the story
进入虚构故事
text: The supplied booklet and event text describe a hospital mystery about a missing medicine.
所提供的剧本册与宣传文本讲述了一个药物失窃的医院谜案。

title: Discuss the clues
交流与推理
text: The plan also lists a medical-themed social deduction game. This was an activity format, not clinical diagnostic training.
方案还列有医学主题社交推理游戏；这是活动形式，并非临床诊断训练。

title: Introduce the health topic
介绍健康知识
text: A short science session was included in the event plan to introduce tuberculosis awareness and prevention.
活动方案安排了简短的科普环节，介绍结核病认识与预防相关知识。

role: I helped plan the interactive health-education activity with the team, connecting the story, game and science session.
我与团队共同参与策划这场互动健康教育活动，衔接故事、游戏与科普环节。
reflection: The activity explored an interactive format for health communication. The supplied records do not establish improved medical knowledge, behaviour or health outcomes.
这次活动探索了互动式健康传播形式；现有记录不足以证明医学知识、行为或健康结果的改善。
evidence: 活动合照、海报与活动方案
evidenceNote: A group photograph documents the activity; the poster and event text describe its design. The story and its missing medicine are fictional.
合照记录活动，海报与宣传文本介绍活动设计；故事情节及其中失窃的药物均属虚构。
actionsHeading: The format described in the event materials
活动材料介绍的三个环节

label: DIALOGUE & WOMEN’S HEALTH
对话与女性健康
title: Pregnancy-related risks: what should public education cover?
妊娠风险：公众教育应涵盖什么？
shortTitle: 妊娠风险与健康科普讨论
summary: A student discussion designed around who should receive information about pregnancy-related risks, what it should cover and who should communicate it.
围绕妊娠风险科普应面向谁、涵盖什么，以及由谁传播，设计学生讨论。
question: What makes health information helpful, balanced and appropriate?
什么样的健康信息，是有帮助、平衡且适当的？
why: The discussion plan connects pregnancy-related health information with informed choice, audience and responsibility for public education.
讨论方案把妊娠相关健康信息与知情选择、受众及公众教育的责任联系起来。

title: Who is the audience?
向谁普及？
text: Should information about pregnancy-related risks, responsibilities and possible consequences reach women beyond those currently planning a pregnancy, including students?
是否应向准备生育者以外的女性群体，包括学生，普及妊娠可能涉及的风险、责任与后果？

title: What should it cover?
普及到何种程度？
text: How much detail should risk communication provide, and how should its accuracy and presentation be considered?
风险科普应提供多深的信息，又应如何考虑其准确性与表达方式？

title: Who should take part?
谁共同参与？
text: Should pregnancy-related health knowledge form part of general education for women and men, especially students, and to what extent?
妊娠相关健康知识是否应纳入面向女性和男性，尤其是学生的通识教育？应深入到何种程度？

role: I helped organise and facilitate the student discussion with the team, focusing on health communication and medical ethics.
我与团队共同参与组织和推动学生讨论，关注健康传播与医学伦理。
reflection: These are questions for discussion. The page does not state a group consensus or provide individual medical advice.
这里呈现的是供讨论的问题，不代表集体共识，也不提供个体医学建议。
evidenceNote: The posters and plans record the topics and proposed format. They do not establish attendance, a consensus or an evaluated educational outcome.
海报与方案记录讨论议题和设计形式，不能据此确认实际人数、形成的共识或经评估的教育结果。
actionsHeading: Three questions in the discussion plan
讨论方案中的三个问题

label: PEER VOICES & EXPRESSION
朋辈声音与表达
title: You don’t have to be a top-ranked student to be heard.
不用排名靠前，也能被大家听见。
summary: Peer Voices invited students to share learning approaches, everyday experiences and reflections without requiring a high academic ranking.
热風朋辈说邀请学生分享学习方法、日常经历与成长思考，不以学业排名靠前作为分享门槛。
question: Whose experience gets to count as something worth sharing?
什么样的经历，才算值得被分享？
why: The programme notes emphasise that students may have useful experiences to share beyond conventional measures of academic achievement.
活动说明强调，传统学业成绩之外的经历与方法，也可以成为有价值的分享内容。

title: Share ways of learning
分享学习方法
text: The invitation welcomed personal learning approaches and practical habits.
活动邀请大家分享个人的学习方法与实用习惯。

title: Talk about experience
讲述个人经历
text: Everyday experiences, interests and reflections on university life were among the suggested topics.
日常经历、兴趣与大学生活反思，都是说明中提出的分享方向。

title: Broaden the invitation
拓宽表达入口
text: The notes explicitly welcomed contributions without making academic rank a condition for speaking.
活动说明明确欢迎不同经验，不把学业排名作为发言条件。

role: I created the platform with the community, making room for students to share what they had learned and how they were growing.
我与社群共同搭建这个平台，为学生分享所学、讲述成长留出空间。
reflection: Meaningful engagement can start with a simple invitation: your experience is worth listening to.
有意义的参与，有时就从一个简单的邀请开始：你的经历，值得被倾听。
evidenceNote: The archived posters and notes describe the invitation to share and proposed topics. They do not provide a participant count or an assessment of personal growth.
存档海报与说明记录了分享初衷和拟议话题，并未提供实际参与人数或个人成长效果评估。
actionsHeading: The invitation in the programme notes
活动说明中的分享邀请

title: Set the direction
发起与定位
text: Founded Hotwind and helped its purpose evolve from a reading salon into a wider community for dialogue, learning and public engagement.
从零发起热風，推动定位从读书沙龙逐步拓展到对话、学习与公众参与。

title: Listen and adapt
倾听与调整
text: Helped review early peer-support ideas and refocus the programme on reading, discussion and public engagement.
参与反思早期朋辈支持构想，推动项目聚焦阅读、讨论与公众参与。

title: Bring the team together
团队与协作
text: Led a nine-member core team and helped coordinate responsibilities, activities and external contacts.
带领9人核心团队，参与协调分工、活动与外部联系。

title: Turn ideas into experiences
策划与执行
text: Helped plan reading activities, health-communication events and public discussions with the team.
与团队共同参与策划阅读活动、健康传播活动与公共讨论。
